title: August and the Orbit
premise: Sable Blackwood, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs cargo between two worlds severed by a decades-old war. When a ship that never flew appears on the manifests carrying Sable's own name—spelled the way their dead mother spelled it—they realize someone is resurrecting erased identities, and Sable's carefully buried past is the key. Pursued by an orbital authority that erases people as easily as records, Sable races to the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast proof of the purge before the signal—and they—are wiped. In the end, Sable must choose between reclaiming a stolen identity and destroying it forever, and chooses to give it away: broadcasting every erased name but their own, surviving as no one at all.
about_author: Felix Hartwell is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction, and his work is known for its quiet, weather-worn prose and characters who love machines more than people. He writes from a coastal town whose location he declines to confirm, insisting only that the fog is load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sable tends the orbital seed-vault garden above Meridian-9, then flies the silent corridor to Vesper Station, where the two worlds' silence is enforced by custom and fear. POV: Sable. Beat: loneliness made routine; we learn what invisibility costs and why Sable chose it.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: A dock clerk's error surfaces a manifest for the Calyx—a ship decommissioned before launch—listing a passenger named Sabine Blackwood, Sable's birth name, erased twenty years ago. POV: Sable. Beat: dread blooming in a mundane moment; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable searches the vault's deep archives for the Calyx's flight plan and finds their mother's handwriting in a terraforming log she never signed. POV: Sable, with archival fragments. Beat: grief resurfacing; identity revealed as something buried alive, not dead.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Names
chapters.summary: Registry officer Ivo Kessler boards Sable's ship for a routine inspection and asks oddly precise questions about the Calyx. Sable lies well, but Kessler leaves a tracker. POV: Sable. Beat: first true threat; power shown as paperwork and patience.

chapters.title: Vesper Doesn't Speak
chapters.summary: On Vesper Station, Sable seeks an old smuggler, Dree, who once flew the Calyx's sister ship. Dree confirms the Calyx carried 'the list'—names purged after the war—and never launched because its crew was erased mid-boarding. POV: Sable. Beat: horror of bureaucratic annihilation; stakes widen beyond one name.

chapters.title: Signal in Dead Space
chapters.summary: A fragmentary broadcast reaches Sable's ship: someone using the Calyx's old callsign, repeating coordinates near the edge relay. It signs off with a lullaby only Sable's mother sang. POV: Sable. Beat: hope weaponized into compulsion; Sable decides to run the route no one flies.

chapters.title: Cargo of Strangers
chapters.summary: Sable takes on legitimate freight as cover but discovers stowaway Juno, a teenage registry archivist fleeing after finding the purge files. POV alternates Sable/Juno. Beat: reluctant alliance; Juno's idealism cracks against Sable's survival cynicism.

chapters.title: Kessler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kessler, revealed via his POV, maintains the ledger of erased names—and is hunting whoever is reactivating them, believing restoration will reignite the war. He flags Sable as an accomplice. POV: Kessler. Beat: antagonist humanized; his corruption framed as duty.

chapters.title: The Burn Corridor
chapters.summary: Pursued by registry cutters, Sable threads the debris fields of the war's last battle, burning fuel and nearly the ship. Juno proves her worth navigating by memorized charts. POV: Sable. Beat: action peak one; trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Graveyard of the Calyx
chapters.summary: They find the Calyx itself, adrift and intact, its passenger cabins sealed—with bodies? No: empty, beds made, meals half-eaten, as if everyone stepped out mid-moment. POV: Sable. Beat: uncanny dread; the erasure was literal, not metaphorical.

chapters.title: Sabine
chapters.summary: Inside the Calyx, Sable finds their mother's final letter: she boarded voluntarily to hide the list inside the ship's quantum core, betting someone would come looking. The letter addresses 'my child, whichever name you wear.' POV: Sable. Beat: emotional core; grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They reach the derelict edge relay and find it occupied: a small community of 'unregistered' survivors—the erased who escaped—led by a woman wearing Sable's mother's face. POV: Sable. Beat: vertigo of belonging; answers arrive wrapped in new questions.

chapters.title: Copies
chapters.summary: The woman, Ash, explains the purge used identity-transfer tech: the erased were copied out and the originals destroyed. She is a copy of Sabine Blackwood. Sable confronts what 'self' means when the original is ash. POV: Sable/Ash. Beat: theme crystallized; identity as data, grief as plagiarism.

chapters.title: Juno's Choice
chapters.summary: Juno decodes the full purge ledger: thousands of names, including living officials who erased rivals. She wants to broadcast everything now; Ash warns the relay lacks range without the Calyx's core. POV: Juno. Beat: moral escalation; knowledge becomes responsibility.

chapters.title: Kessler Arrives
chapters.summary: Kessler's cutter docks at the relay under truce flag. He offers Sable amnesty and erasure of their file—in exchange for the core and the list. He genuinely believes he is preventing a second war. POV: Kessler/Sable. Beat: temptation scene; the devil offers peace.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The unregistered community votes: surrender the core and stay hidden, or fight to broadcast and be hunted. Old wounds split them; Ash abstains, saying she has already died once. POV: ensemble. Beat: democracy under pressure; the price of survival made collective.

chapters.title: What Sable Steals
chapters.summary: Sable secretly copies the ledger and sabotages the core's handoff, forcing Kessler's withdrawal—but Juno catches them and feels betrayed by the deception. POV: Sable. Beat: protagonist's corruption arc; becoming what they fled.

chapters.title: Calyx Rising
chapters.summary: Sable, Juno, and volunteers fly the ghost ship itself, cold-starting engines sealed for twenty years, while Kessler's fleet converges. POV: Sable. Beat: rising climax; the dead ship given a purpose posthumously.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: At maximum range, they transmit the full purge ledger toward both worlds' public nets. Kessler's flagship locks weapons; Juno reroutes power from life support to the antenna. POV: Juno. Beat: climax; truth sent at the cost of air.

chapters.title: The Price of the Signal
chapters.summary: The broadcast lands; both worlds erupt. But the transmitter burn kills the Calyx's systems, and Ash stays aboard to hold the antenna alignment as the ship drifts into dead space, dying a second time so the names live. POV: Sable. Beat: sacrifice; the copy outlives the original's meaning.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Weeks later, both worlds hold public readings of the restored names. Kessler, arrested, asks Sable whether it was worth it; Sable cannot answer cleanly. Juno departs to rebuild the archives honestly. POV: Sable. Beat: bittersweet reckoning; victory that doesn't feel clean.

chapters.title: August and the Orbit
chapters.summary: Sable returns to the seed-vault garden in high summer, planting for colonists who will now actually come, under a name they choose fresh rather than inherited or erased. They keep one thing from Sabine: the lullaby, hummed to seedlings. POV: Sable. Beat: resolution; identity as a garden—tended, chosen, alive.
